titel: #217 Introduction to René-Robert Cavelier, Sieur de La Salle
einzeiler: The early life and expeditions of French explorer René-Robert Cavelier, Sieur de La Salle
kurzfassung: This episode explores the life of the ambitious and driven French explorer René-Robert Cavelier, Sieur de La Salle. It examines the complex geopolitical landscape of 17th-century North America, involving France, England, Spain, and indigenous nations. The narrative follows La Salle's early days in New France, his rigorous Jesuit training, and his grueling initial expeditions into the wilderness.
stichpunkte: Introduction to La Salle and the numerous American landmarks and places named in his honor
Geopolitical overview of North America in the late 17th century involving France, England, Spain, and the Iroquois Confederacy
La Salle's background in Rouen, France, his education by the Jesuits, and his departure from the religious order
Establishment of La Salle's estate near Montreal and his rigorous self-training in survival and indigenous languages
Planning and launching of La Salle's first major expedition alongside Sulpician missionaries
Extreme physical hardships of traveling the turbulent waterways and portages of New France
Cultural encounters with local tribes, including witness accounts of rituals and ceremonies
Historians' debate regarding whether La Salle actually reached the Ohio River and Pittsburgh
Desertion of crew members, La Salle's survival with his companion Nika, and his return to Montreal

clips.hook: Why do so many places bear his name?
clips.text: The primary achievement attributed to the explorer, reaching the mouth of the Mississippi River in 1682, had already been accomplished by previous explorers decades earlier.

clips.hook: A massive demographic imbalance in early Canada
clips.text: A census from 1666 recorded just over 3,200 Europeans living in the settlements along the St. Lawrence River, which was a tiny fraction compared to the English colonial population.

clips.hook: A chance encounter leads to a massive land grant
clips.text: During the transatlantic crossing, the future explorer spent extensive time conversing with a senior religious leader, which resulted in receiving a large tract of land near Montreal upon arrival.

clips.hook: Separated from death by a mere breath
clips.text: Navigating the treacherous and raging waterways required travelers to walk directly through freezing, violent currents while carrying their heavy boats and belongings.

clips.hook: Left completely alone in the wilderness
clips.text: Following months of growing resentment over slow progress and harsh conditions, all of the expedition's guides and porters abandoned the leader overnight.

beschreibung:
It is time to get back to New France and the exploration of the middle of this beautiful country of ours. Our vehicle will René-Robert Cavelier, Sieur de La Salle, known to both his contemporaries and to history as “La Salle.” You’ve heard his name, especially if you live within driving distance of the Mississippi, but do you know what he actually did? This and the next few episodes tell La Salle’s remarkable story.

We are back in New France, along the St. Lawrence River, now in the 1660s. The episode begins with an introduction to the geopolitics of North America from the French perspective, then pivots to La Salle’s early life and first years in New France, where he had received a grant of land on roughly the site of Montreal’s international airport. Finally, we conclude with his first journey of discovery, an attempt – perhaps fulfilled – to discover the Ohio River, of which he had heard from Seneca Iroquois who wintered with him in 1668-69. This voyage mattered, because it might have established French claims to the Pittsburgh area, the ambiguity of which was, along with George Washington, the catalyst for the French and Indian War. Sadly, those claims were ambiguous because the French national archives had misplaced the relevant narratives, and they only resurfaced in the 19th century. Archivists matter!
